clue.text: Pass one of the basic subjects a head provided

parts.note: the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic) are the basic subjects, so one of them is R
'a head' means per person, as in 'a pound each'

explanation.surface: A pupil scrapes through one of the core subjects, with every head teacher's blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' is a verb here, as in 'pass me the salt', not an exam result; 'provided' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand something over across a table is to stretch out and give it, a common verb sense.

clue.text: Dreadful rattiness seen in fighting

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters of rattiness are in a terrible mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bad temper is evident in a combatant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges RATTINESS; 'seen in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing or standing up against something is fighting back, as in a wartime movement of opposition.

clue.text: Violent struggle in a resort city in US

parts.note: to resort to a place is to go there
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out in an American holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'resort' is a verb, not a holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme anguish or a death throe, originally from the Greek for contest or struggle.

clue.text: Tricky assignment nobody wants to handle

definitions.text: Tricky assignment nobody wants to handle

parts.words: Tricky assignment nobody wants to handle
parts.note: an awkward issue likened to a scalding baked vegetable that nobody will pick up

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a controversial issue passed quickly from person to person, like something too hot to hold.

clue.text: Chief source of interest

explanation.surface: The head of a firm is where the money flows from.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means main or foremost; as a noun it is the capital sum a loan or deposit earns interest on.

clue.text: Secure place for a tiny literary work, writer concludes

indicators.note: 'concludes' puts the writer at the end of the answer

parts.note: a play is a work for the stage
a pen is something to write with

explanation.surface: A small literary piece is finished off safely by its author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tiny' is a tiny child, a toddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fenced enclosure where a toddler can be left safely to amuse itself.

clue.text: Invest in small business

parts.note: a stall is a small trading booth

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into a little shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' suggests money; it means to put someone into office formally.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a person in office with ceremony, as a bishop is inducted.

clue.text: Retired sailor? Explorer

explanation.surface: A seaman now ashore is also an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is cryptic: a sailor (AB, able seaman) gone to bed, inside a COT.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Venetian navigator who reached North America in 1497; an able seaman in a bed has turned in.

clue.text: Clearly communicated how to vote

explanation.surface: Instructions on casting a ballot were explained plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an idea over to listeners is to convey it; on a British ballot paper you mark an X against your choice.

clue.text: Trusty new ally combined with old

indicators.note: new says the letters of ally and the old one are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A dependable fresh partner is teamed up with a former one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combined with' is a link; 'new' rearranges ALLY with O.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful and true to a cause or friend.

clue.text: Recklessly cut across army vehicles

indicators.note: done recklessly, the letters of 'cut across' are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver carelessly swerves over a road full of military trucks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recklessly' turns CUTACROSS into the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Light armoured reconnaissance trucks used by armies are known by this name.

clue.text: Be a tease — why? Sounds crazy!

indicators.note: 'sounds' says the letters named by the words before it are spoken, not written

parts.note: said aloud: the letter B, the letter A, 'tease' heard as T's (two Ts), and 'why' as the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why another person keeps teasing, and finds it mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the words as letter names: B, A, T's, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial British word for mad or eccentric, from having bats in the belfry.

clue.text: Authority makes no pronouncements, apparently

parts.note: 'says' as a plural noun are statements or pronouncements
O looks like zero, so 'no' or nothing gives O

explanation.surface: A silent official appears to exert power without speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' and 'apparently' are links: read the phrase as SAYS O, 'says nothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the final word means having the power to decide, as in 'on whose authority?'.

clue.text: Sort of exam academic may be opposed to

explanation.surface: A test format that a scholar might object to.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on exam tests skills rather than writing; 'practical' is the usual opposite of theoretical or academic.

clue.text: Volunteer to stop Jack and Mark

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, as is an AB, able seaman
a stain is a mark or blemish

explanation.surface: Two men named Jack and Mark offer to stop something.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Mark look like two people's names; they are a sailor and a blot.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain by choice from drinking or voting is to hold back voluntarily.

clue.text: Shooting not allowed in a certain season

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece within the other

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
in cricket and tennis a ball or batsman ruled out is not allowed

explanation.surface: Hunting is banned during a particular time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns; it means plants putting out new growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing new buds and shoots, as plants do.

clue.text: Light nothing in addition to squib

parts.note: a lamp is a light
O resembles zero, i.e. nothing
'on' means added on, as in 'a tax on top of that'

explanation.surface: A firework that gives no light, adding to the disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: A squib is both a small firework, the surface sense, and a short satirical piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A short piece of satire ridiculing someone is a lampoon or skit.

clue.text: Do extra work that's naturally illuminating

explanation.surface: Someone takes a second job that sheds light on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a second job, often secretly at night, is one sense; the glow from the night sky's satellite is the other.

clue.text: Feeling less honour's apparent in politician's address

parts.note: 'number' read as more numb, having less feeling
in bridge the ten is one of the honour cards (ace, king, queen, jack, ten)

explanation.surface: A minister's speech reveals numbness and a lack of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' suggests a speech; it means a street address, 10 Downing Street, the Prime Minister's home. 'apparent' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The London residence of the British Prime Minister is known by its door number.

clue.text: Dismiss parade

explanation.surface: An officer sends troops off after inspecting them.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone out or expel them is one sense; an assembly of people, or troops called out on parade, is the other.

clue.text: Sir Lucius, none the less, set off

indicators.note: 'the less' says the O is taken away from the name

parts.note: Sir Lucius O'Trigger is the duelling Irishman in Sheridan's play The Rivals
O, looking like zero, stands for none

explanation.surface: A character, nevertheless, departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'none the less' looks like 'nevertheless'; it means O removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To spark off or start something, like a gun's firing lever.

clue.text: May, for example, flourish and prosper

explanation.surface: A woman named May thrives and does well.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like a woman's name or the month; it is hawthorn flower, called may in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn flowers (may) are a kind of bloom; to bloom or come into flower also means to thrive.

clue.text: Characteristic of short delivery — bowled it very badly

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: badly says the letters of 'it very' are put in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A cricketer's short ball was bowled very poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests a cricket ball; it means speech. 'badly' turns ITVERY into REVITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Conciseness or shortness of speech, as in 'the soul of wit'.

clue.text: Jolly queue in America? Bob may be held up by it

definitions.text: Bob may be held up by it

parts.note: 'jolly' as an adverb means very or completely, as does 'plumb' (plumb crazy)
Americans call a queue a line

explanation.surface: A cheerful American queue, where a man named Bob might be delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name; it is the weight on a builder's vertical cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb bob is the lead weight hanging on the cord builders use to check vertical.

clue.text: Person with pretensions can be a problem

explanation.surface: A show-off can be troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy affected person is one sense; a puzzling question is the other.

clue.text: He remains after Don leaves town

indicators.note: when Don leaves, those letters are removed from the town's name

parts.note: Basildon is a new town in Essex, England
Don taken as written

explanation.surface: A man stays on after another man departs from a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Don looks like a man's name or a lecturer; 'remains' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so a fitting stand-in for a pronoun meaning one male person.

clue.text: A bit of a shock, we hear, for philosopher

indicators.note: 'we hear' says the word is taken by its sound only

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mass of it, and a lock is a bit of hair

explanation.surface: Someone is told something mildly surprising about a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests surprise; it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was the 17th-century English empiricist thinker.

clue.text: Arrest for attack on king

explanation.surface: A police officer seizes someone for assaulting the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or restrain is one sense; in chess, a direct threat to the opponent's monarch is the other.

clue.text: Tell, for example, stories with incredibly sad, slow beginnings

indicators.note: the beginnings of the five words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A storyteller recounts tales with unbelievably mournful, slow openings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb; it is William Tell, the legendary hero of Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell, the crossbowman of legend, was from Switzerland, so he is one example of its people.

clue.text: Taking young man's advice and becoming lost

explanation.surface: A youth follows advice and loses his way.
explanation.walkthrough: The advice is 'Go west, young man', a saying linked to the American frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading towards the setting sun follows that frontier advice; the phrase is also slang for being lost, broken or dead.

clue.text: Returned pistol to Lear's uncle in normal way

indicators.note: returned means the pistol's name is read backwards

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
Edward Lear wrote the nonsense poem about 'my Uncle Arly'

explanation.surface: A pistol is handed back to King Lear's relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear suggests Shakespeare's king; it is the nonsense poet Edward Lear. 'Returned' turns LUGER into REGUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something habitually and as usual, by the normal routine, is acting as a rule.

clue.text: Captured a king in 17

indicators.note: 'in' puts the letters for a king inside the other piece

parts.note: the 17-down answer, whose second word is the number after nine
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch was seized at the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 refers to the answer at 17-down; only its second word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Seized or caught is the past participle of the verb, as a prisoner is held.
